Documents are plain JSON objects. Add them in batches, update a few fields at a time and track each change as a task.

A document is one JSON object in an index: a product, an article, a support ticket. ZeroIndex does not need a schema. Every document needs a unique primary key, and every other field is up to you.

```json
{
  "id": 1042,
  "name": "Wireless headphones",
  "brand": "Nordvik",
  "category": "Audio",
  "price": 129,
  "in_stock": true,
  "tags": ["bluetooth", "noise cancelling"]
}
```

## Field types

ZeroIndex searches strings and arrays of strings. Numbers, booleans and dates can be filtered and sorted once you mark them in the index settings. Nested objects are flattened, so `dimensions.width` becomes its own field.

<Callout type="tip" title="Dates">
  Store dates as Unix timestamps in seconds. They sort and filter as plain numbers.
</Callout>

## Adding and replacing

Send documents in an array. If a document with the same primary key already exists, it is replaced in full.

<CodeGroup labels={["cURL", "JavaScript", "Python"]}>

```bash
curl https://api.zeroindex.test/v1/indexes/products/documents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZEROINDEX_KEY" \
  -d '[{ "id": 1042, "name": "Wireless headphones", "price": 129 }]'
```

```js
await client.index("products").addDocuments([
  { id: 1042, name: "Wireless headphones", price: 129 },
]);
```

```python
client.index("products").add_documents([
    {"id": 1042, "name": "Wireless headphones", "price": 129},
])
```

</CodeGroup>

## Updating some fields

To change only some fields, use `updateDocuments`. Fields you leave out keep their current value.

```js
await client.index("products").updateDocuments([{ id: 1042, price: 99 }]);
```

## Tasks

Writes are asynchronous. Every add, update or delete returns a task straight away, and the change is searchable once the task succeeds, usually in under a second.

```json
{
  "taskUid": 8812,
  "indexUid": "products",
  "status": "enqueued",
  "type": "documentAdditionOrUpdate",
  "enqueuedAt": "2026-10-11T09:14:02Z"
}
```

Wait for a task when the next step depends on it, for example in a test:

```js
const task = await client.index("products").addDocuments(documents);
await client.waitForTask(task.taskUid);
```

## Batches

Send up to 1,000 documents or 10 MB per request, whichever comes first. For larger imports, split the documents into batches and send them one after another. Tasks on the same index run in order.

## Deleting

```js
await client.index("products").deleteDocument(1042);
await client.index("products").deleteDocuments({ filter: "in_stock = false" });
```

<Callout type="danger">
  A delete by filter removes every matching document. Run the same filter as a search first to see what it matches.
</Callout>
Narrow results by any field you mark as filterable, with a short expression language that reads like SQL.

A filter limits a search to documents that match a condition, like a category or a price range. Filters do not change the ranking. They only decide which documents are in the results.

## Making a field filterable

List the field in `filterableAttributes` first. Filtering on any other field returns an `invalid_filter` error.

```js
await client.index("products").updateSettings({
  filterableAttributes: ["category", "brand", "price", "in_stock"],
});
```

## Writing a filter

<CodeGroup labels={["cURL", "JavaScript", "Python"]}>

```bash
curl https://api.zeroindex.test/v1/indexes/products/search \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZEROINDEX_KEY" \
  -d '{ "q": "headphones", "filter": "category = Audio AND price < 150" }'
```

```js
await client.index("products").search("headphones", {
  filter: "category = Audio AND price < 150",
});
```

```python
client.index("products").search("headphones", {
    "filter": "category = Audio AND price < 150",
})
```

</CodeGroup>

## Operators

| Operator | Example |
| --- | --- |
| `=` and `!=` | `brand = Nordvik` |
| `>`, `>=`, `<` and `<=` | `price >= 50` |
| `TO` | `price 50 TO 150` |
| `IN` | `category IN [Audio, Lighting]` |
| `EXISTS` | `discount EXISTS` |
| `AND`, `OR` and `NOT` | `in_stock = true AND NOT brand = Nordvik` |

Use parentheses to group conditions, and quotes around values with spaces: `brand = "Casa Bruna"`.

## Filtering arrays

When a field holds an array, a condition matches if any value in it matches. `tags = bluetooth` finds every document whose `tags` contain `bluetooth`.

<Callout type="note">
  Filters run before ranking and add almost no time to a search, even on millions of documents.
</Callout>

## Filters on the server

To make sure a user only ever sees their own documents, do not trust a filter sent from the browser. Put it in a scoped key instead, as shown in [Authentication](/docs/getting-started/authentication).
An index holds one kind of document, like products or articles, along with the settings that decide how it is searched.

An index is a collection of documents that you search together. Most apps have one index per kind of thing people look for: `products`, `articles`, `customers`. Each index has its own documents, its own settings and its own search endpoint.

## Creating an index

You do not have to create an index before using it. The first time you add documents to a name that does not exist, ZeroIndex creates the index for you with the default settings. Create one explicitly when you want to choose the primary key or apply settings before any documents arrive.

<CodeGroup labels={["cURL", "JavaScript", "Python"]}>

```bash
curl https://api.zeroindex.test/v1/indexes \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZEROINDEX_KEY" \
  -d '{ "uid": "products", "primaryKey": "id" }'
```

```js
await client.createIndex("products", { primaryKey: "id" });
```

```python
client.create_index("products", primary_key="id")
```

</CodeGroup>

<ParamField name="uid" type="string" required>
  The name of the index. Use lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores, up to 64 characters.
</ParamField>
<ParamField name="primaryKey" type="string" default="id">
  The field that uniquely identifies each document. It cannot be changed once the index has documents.
</ParamField>

## Settings

Settings control what is searchable, what can be filtered and how results are ranked. They apply to the whole index, and changing them rebuilds it in the background.

```js
await client.index("products").updateSettings({
  searchableAttributes: ["name", "brand", "description"],
  filterableAttributes: ["category", "price", "in_stock"],
  sortableAttributes: ["price", "created_at"],
});
```

<ResponseField name="searchableAttributes" type="string[]">
  The fields that queries match against, most important first. Defaults to every field.
</ResponseField>
<ResponseField name="filterableAttributes" type="string[]">
  The fields you can use in filters and facets. Empty by default.
</ResponseField>
<ResponseField name="sortableAttributes" type="string[]">
  The fields you can sort results by. Empty by default.
</ResponseField>

<Callout type="warning">
  Rebuilding a large index can take a few minutes. Searches keep working on the old settings until the new ones are ready.
</Callout>

## Limits

| | Free | Pro |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Indexes | 10 | Unlimited |
| Documents per index | 100,000 | 50 million |
| Size of one document | 100 KB | 1 MB |

Results are ordered by a list of rules, applied one after another. Change the order or add your own to fit your content.

When a query matches many documents, ZeroIndex sorts them with a list of ranking rules. The first rule sorts everything. Each next rule only breaks ties left by the ones before it.

## Default rules

<Steps>
  <Step title="Words">
    Documents that match more of the query words come first.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Typo">
    Documents with fewer typos come first. `headphones` beats `hedphones`.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Proximity">
    Documents where the query words sit closer together come first.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Attribute">
    Matches in more important fields come first, in the order of `searchableAttributes`.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Exactness">
    Documents that match the query exactly come before those that only match a prefix.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Custom rules

Add a rule that sorts by a number to push popular or recent documents up. The field must be listed in `sortableAttributes`.

```js
await client.index("products").updateSettings({
  rankingRules: ["words", "typo", "proximity", "attribute", "exactness", "sales_count:desc"],
});
```

<Callout type="tip">
  Put custom rules last. If they come first, a best seller that barely matches the query can beat a product that matches it exactly.
</Callout>

## Typo tolerance

ZeroIndex allows one typo in words of five letters or more, and two typos in words of nine letters or more. You can change both thresholds, or turn typos off for fields like product codes.

```js
await client.index("products").updateSettings({
  typoTolerance: {
    minWordSizeForTypos: { oneTypo: 4, twoTypos: 8 },
    disableOnAttributes: ["sku"],
  },
});
```

## Seeing why a result ranks where it does

Pass `showRankingScore` to get a score between 0 and 1 for every hit. It is useful while tuning, but do not show it to users.

```js
const { hits } = await client.index("products").search("wireless", { showRankingScore: true });
// hits[0]._rankingScore === 0.97
```
Every request needs an API key. Use admin keys on your server and search keys everywhere else.

ZeroIndex uses bearer tokens. Send your key in the `Authorization` header of every request.

```bash
curl https://api.zeroindex.test/v1/indexes \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer zi_admin_4f8a2c91e7"
```

## Header

<ParamField name="Authorization" type="string" required>
  The word `Bearer`, a space and your API key.
</ParamField>

## Kinds of keys

There are two kinds of keys. You can create as many of each as you need.

- **Admin keys** start with `zi_admin_`. They can create and delete indexes, change settings and add documents.
- **Search keys** start with `zi_search_`. They can only search, so they are safe to use in a browser or a mobile app.

<Callout type="danger" title="Keep admin keys secret">
  Anyone with an admin key can delete your indexes. If one leaks, revoke it in the dashboard straight away and create a new one.
</Callout>

## Scoped search keys

A scoped key limits a search key to some indexes or adds a filter to every query. Use one to make sure each customer only sees their own documents.

```js
const key = client.keys.createScoped({
  parent: process.env.ZEROINDEX_SEARCH_KEY,
  indexes: ["tickets"],
  filter: "account_id = 4821",
  expiresIn: "1h",
});
```

## Questions

<Accordion title="How many keys can I create?">
  As many as you like. Most teams use one admin key per server and one search key per app.
</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Can I rotate a key without downtime?">
  Yes. Create the new key, deploy it, then revoke the old one. Both work until you revoke.
</Accordion>
<Accordion title="Do keys expire?">
  Admin and search keys never expire. Scoped keys expire after the time you set, up to 30 days.
</Accordion>
ZeroIndex is a search API. Send it your content and get fast, typo tolerant search back in a single request.

ZeroIndex takes the content you already have, like products, articles or support tickets, and turns it into a search index you can query in milliseconds. There are no servers to run and no ranking rules to write before your first result.

<Callout type="tip" title="New here?">
  The [quickstart](/docs/getting-started/quickstart) takes about five minutes and ends with a working search box.
</Callout>

## How it works

You create an **index**, add **documents** to it as JSON and send **queries**. ZeroIndex handles typos, synonyms and ranking, and returns the best matches with the matching words highlighted.

<CodeGroup labels={["cURL", "JavaScript", "Python"]}>

```bash
curl https://api.zeroindex.test/v1/indexes/products/search \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZEROINDEX_KEY" \
  -d '{ "q": "wireless hedphones" }'
```

```js
import { ZeroIndex } from "@zeroindex/client";

const client = new ZeroIndex(process.env.ZEROINDEX_KEY);
const results = await client.index("products").search("wireless hedphones");
```

```python
import os
from zeroindex import ZeroIndex

client = ZeroIndex(os.environ["ZEROINDEX_KEY"])
results = client.index("products").search("wireless hedphones")
```

</CodeGroup>

The query above has a typo on purpose. ZeroIndex still puts wireless headphones first.

## What you get

- **Results in under 50 ms**, from a region close to your users.
- **Typo tolerance** that works out of the box, in every language.
- **Filters and facets** for price ranges, categories and anything else in your documents.
- **Keys you can scope** to one index, one action or one customer.

```js
import { ZeroIndex } from "@zeroindex/client";

]);
```
